title: Emilia-Romagna's Pump Prices Cool Off While LPG and Natural Gas Keep Climbing
dek: Benzina and Gasolio have given back most of their September spike in Emilia-Romagna, but GPL and Metano are still rising — and rising faster locally than nationally.
executive_summary: As of November 23, 2026, self-service Benzina in Emilia-Romagna averages €1.9608/L, Gasolio €2.2278/L, GPL €0.8375/L and Metano €2.1128/L — all four sitting fractionally above the national self-service averages of €1.9561/L, €2.2264/L, €0.8329/L and €2.1072/L. Day over day, the region barely moved: Benzina and Gasolio each eased by about a tenth of a cent, while GPL and Metano held exactly where they finished the day before, across 1,732 of the region's 1,882 registered stations reporting prices.

Zoom out to the eighteen weeks tracked since July 20, and a sharper story emerges. Benzina and Gasolio both round-tripped — climbing through late summer to a peak in the week of September 21 (Benzina €2.167/L, Gasolio €2.3691/L regionally), then sliding back to levels close to where they started. GPL and Metano, by contrast, have kept climbing: regional GPL is up 10.2% since tracking began and Metano has risen 43.1% over the same period — in both cases outpacing the national increase (9.7% and 40.5% respectively). Emilia-Romagna's heating-adjacent fuels are drifting upward faster than the rest of Italy even as its road fuels retrace most of their autumn run-up.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Settles Near Its Lowest Point in Months, Just Above the National Line
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Emilia-Romagna closed November 23 at €1.9608/L, down a fraction of a cent from €1.961/L the day before. That puts the region 0.24% above the €1.9561/L national self-service average — a small premium that has held for the past few weeks.

The wider trend is a round trip. Regional Benzina opened the tracked period (week of July 20) at €1.9736/L, climbed through the summer to a peak of €2.167/L in the week of September 21 — a 9.8% rise — then gave almost all of it back, falling 9.5% from that peak to today's €1.9608/L. The national average followed the same arc (€1.9756/L to €2.1669/L to €1.9561/L) but fell slightly further from its peak (-9.7% vs Emilia-Romagna's -9.5%), which is why the region now sits marginally above the national line after moving in near lockstep all autumn.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio Retreats From Its September Peak, Trading Within a Cent of Italy
paragraphs: Gasolio self-service averaged €2.2278/L in Emilia-Romagna on November 23, down slightly from €2.2281/L the previous day — just €0.0014/L, or 0.06%, above the €2.2264/L national average, one of the tightest regional-national gaps of the four fuels tracked.

Like Benzina, Gasolio spiked hard in September: the region hit €2.3691/L in the week of September 21, a 9.2% climb from its July 20 starting point of €2.1695/L, before retreating 6.0% to today's level. Nationally the peak-to-trough move was a slightly larger 6.2% decline, so Emilia-Romagna has given back a touch less of its September run-up than Italy overall — leaving it almost exactly on top of the national average rather than below it, where it sat for most of the summer.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Keeps Climbing, and Emilia-Romagna Is Outpacing the National Rise
paragraphs: GPL self-service in Emilia-Romagna held at €0.8375/L for a second straight day, 0.55% above the €0.8329/L national average — one of the widest regional premiums among the four fuels today.

GPL spent the summer broadly flat in the region, drifting between €0.7475/L and €0.761/L through late September, before turning sharply upward: Emilia-Romagna's GPL rose 10.1% in the eight weeks from September 28 to today, almost identical to the 10.1% national rise over the same stretch. But looked at across the full tracking period since July 20, regional GPL is up 10.2% against 9.7% nationally — a modest, consistent premium in the pace of the increase, not just the price level, that has built up gradually rather than in a single recent jump.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano's Rise Is the Story of the Season — Up 43% Regionally Since July
paragraphs: Metano self-service in Emilia-Romagna was unchanged on the day at €2.1128/L, 0.27% above the €2.1072/L national average.

No fuel in this dataset has moved more. Regional Metano has climbed from €1.4763/L in the week of July 20 to €2.1128/L today — a 43.1% increase over roughly four months — compared with a 40.5% national increase over the same period (€1.4999/L to €2.1072/L). That 2.6-percentage-point gap is the largest regional-vs-national divergence of any fuel tracked here, meaning Emilia-Romagna motorists running on natural gas have seen their relative cost disadvantage against the rest of the country widen through the autumn rather than narrow.

network_section.heading: 1,732 of 1,882 Registered Stations Reported Today — a Stronger Showing Than the National Average
paragraphs: Emilia-Romagna has 1,882 registered fuel stations in the MIMIT registry, of which 1,732 reported prices on November 23 — a 92.0% reporting rate, unchanged from the day before.

That compares with a 90.4% reporting rate nationally (21,679 of 23,977 registered stations). A higher reporting rate generally means the regional averages in this report rest on a broader, more representative slice of the local market than the national figure draws from proportionally — though both rates are high enough that day-to-day price comparisons stay reliable.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: No Spreadsheet, No Manual Update
paragraphs: Every part of this report — pulling the day's price and station data from Italy's MIMIT registry, selecting today's featured region on a self-correcting alphabetical rotation, computing the week-over-week trend lines for all four fuels against the national average, and writing the prose above — runs automatically each morning through an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code.

Contrast that with the alternative: a manually maintained spreadsheet that someone has to open, re-download data into, recalculate, and write up by hand — a process that rarely scales past a handful of regions and tends to lapse the first time the person maintaining it is busy or on holiday. This pipeline updates twenty regions' worth of history every day without anyone touching a spreadsheet.

caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Emilia-Romagna.

The standout number isn't at the pump today — it's in the trend. Emilia-Romagna's Metano (natural gas) price has climbed 43.1% since late July, outpacing the 40.5% rise nationally, while regional GPL is up 10.2% against Italy's 9.7% over the same stretch. Both fuels keep drifting upward faster locally than nationally, even as Benzina and Gasolio have given back most of their September spike and settled back near summer levels.

Fuel Dashboard is a fully automated project: it pulls Italy's daily MIMIT fuel-price registry, spotlights a new region every day on a fixed rotation, computes the weekly trend for every fuel against the national average, and writes up a report like this one — all without a human touching a spreadsheet. It's a live demonstration of what's possible when you use an AI coding tool like Claude Code to build and maintain a real data pipeline instead of a manually updated Excel file: it runs every single day, scales to every region and every fuel, and never falls behind because someone was busy.
